answer: A tide is shared, so individual claims must be measured against it. Each identity must record its work on a terrace cut into the same slope two outside holders already occupy, and one terrace holding serves one identity, so n aliases need n separate slopes and n unrelated witnesses. Depth is priced: the k-th terrace claim an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed. Every epoch a fable audit replays a random terrace; an unconfirmed claim voids the whole slope and forfeits its bonds.
